title: Certificates of Deposit: Dating a Penalized Withdrawal to the Grace Period
content:
Across PCB Certificates of Deposit, a penalty is posted on the same business day as the withdrawal that incurred it. That makes the penalty's posting date a reliable date for the withdrawal itself, and it is the date used to decide whether the withdrawal happened in grace.

## Rule

The withdrawal was made during the grace period when the posting date of its penalty falls on any of the grace days: day 1 up to and including the day numbered by the tier's grace days, where day 1 is the day after the certificate's maturity date.

A posting date on the maturity date itself, or earlier, or after the last grace day, does not place the withdrawal in grace.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical: maturity date 12 September, ten grace days assumed)

| Penalty posting date | Day count from the day after maturity | Withdrawal in grace? |
|---|---|---|
| 12 September | the maturity date itself | No |
| 13 September | day 1 | Yes |
| 22 September | day 10 | Yes, the last grace day |
| 23 September | day 11 | No |

## Point of judgement

**The withdrawal entry is labelled as an early full withdrawal, but its penalty posted on day 4 after maturity.** The dating rule looks only at the posting date, so the withdrawal counts as made in grace.
